data.title: A Ring in the Chowder
data.rumour: Marisol found a ring in the chowder pot. Swears it wasn't hers.
about: A very short, warm story. Marisol from the Clam Shack found a ring at the bottom of the chowder pot, engraved R & J 1975, and sells it to you (§{chowderFind}). The bartender at the Anchor says it's Ray Tibbets's wedding ring, lost in a bowl of chowder on his honeymoon fifty years ago, and the Tibbets' fiftieth anniversary lunch is this week.
At the lunch at the Grange (§{chowderParty}) give Ray the ring during the toasts (Fifty Years), or keep quiet and keep it. Keeping it, or selling it on, is Melted Down.

chowderRing.name: The chowder ring
tells: Gold, worn thin on one side. Engraved inside: R & J 1975.

overheard.line: Laughing: "Marisol found a ring in the chowder pot. Swears it wasn't hers. She's checked everybody's fingers twice."

chowderFind.title: Marisol found a ring in the chowder

text: Marisol Duarte. I cook at the Clam Shack. This was at the bottom of the chowder pot this morning, and before you ask: not mine. Not anybody's in the kitchen.
Is it worth anything? Because if nobody claims it, I'm buying new knives.

then.text: Fine. I'll keep it in the tip jar until someone weeps over it.

steps.text: Oh, and Sully at the Anchor swears R and J is Ray and June Tibbets. Ray lost his wedding ring on their honeymoon. Here. In our restaurant. Fifty years ago.
Their fiftieth is a lunch at the Grange Hall, {when:chowder-party|or:this week}. Just saying.

steps.toast: Calendar: the Tibbets' fiftieth, the Grange Hall, {when:chowder-party} at noon

steps.narrate: The Grange Hall at noon: a sheet cake, a slideshow nobody can make work, and eighty people in their good sweaters.

steps.text: Fifty years! She said yes in 1975 and she's never once let me forget the ring. Lost it in a bowl of chowder on our honeymoon, folks. Right here in Hollow Neck.
He went back for it every summer for ten years. Ate a lot of chowder.

then.narrate: You think about the ring you sold on, and clap along with everyone else.

choose.label: Give Ray the ring, during the toasts

then.narrate: You hand it over between the second toast and the third. Ray reads the inside of the ring and sits down very suddenly.

then.text: Oh, Raymond. Oh, it's the same one.

then.with: Ray Tibbets paid you back for the ring

then.text: No, you're taking the {ring.paid} dollars. Don't argue with a man on his anniversary.

choose.label: Keep quiet. It's just a ring, and it's yours now.

then.narrate: June cuts the cake. You have a slice. It's very good cake, and you don't enjoy it at all.

epilogue.line: Ray Tibbets wears his wedding ring on a chain now, so it can't fall in anything.
Somewhere, a ring engraved R & J 1975 was melted down for scrap. June Tibbets never knew how close it came.
